beats: Same seventy thousand dollar salary. Last year a refund, this year you owe. Why?
Year one: one job, plus a six thousand dollar RRSP. At about thirty-three percent, that's a refund of about two thousand dollars.
Year two: same job, no RRSP. Payroll is built to land close to your actual tax. Refund: almost zero.
Year three: two jobs, thirty-five thousand each. Both payrolls give you the basic personal amount. Under-withheld: about fifty-three hundred dollars.
The twist: your tax barely moved. What changed was what got withheld. A refund isn't a bonus. It's your own money coming back.
Compare box twenty-two on your T4 with the total payable on your notice. Two jobs? On the second TD1, claim zero.
